original_question: What should I restock in my stores next week?

current_process.text: I normally use last month's sales to work out what we need for the week.

customer_context.original_question: What should I restock in my stores next week?

attribution: Data analyst refinement; original customer wording above unchanged
decision: Generate November 30 orders in product units for December 1-7, covering supplier lead time plus seven-day review, using supplied stock, dated incoming orders, safety stock, minimums and multiples.
routine: Load and validate current files; clean recorded sales; estimate demand; subtract usable stock and timely incoming units; apply supplied rules; export all 336 rows and timing exceptions. Replaces repeated aggregation and quantity arithmetic; exact incumbent conversion, return handling and rounding are unknown.
facts: Current process uses last month's sales
Supplied operational files are scenario facts
All operating keys match the 28 products and 12 stores in sales
Stock is an as-of snapshot, not historical exposure
interpretations: Forecast recorded fulfilled outbound units rather than unobserved unconstrained demand
Use a recent-month-rate baseline as an analytical interpretation, not an exact replica of the customer's process
unknowns: Lost sales, inventory availability history, reusable returns, historical order-status changes
Precise incumbent formula, business error costs and availability-versus-excess priority
Independent meaningful improvement threshold and untouched evaluation outcomes

candidate_rationale.recent_month: Fair calendar-month baseline linked to supplied process description
candidate_rationale.recent90: Sparse series support a longer averaging window
candidate_rationale.pooled90: 336 sparse series permit product/store pooling with shrinkage
candidate_rationale.ridge: Low-dimensional pooled regularized autoregression can learn recent demand and annual seasonality without heavy models

evidence: released/input-4.csv: 17,406 rows, all 1,430 calendar dates represented; 42 exact duplicate rows
released/input-1.csv: coverage horizons 8-14 days, seven-day reviews
released/input-2.csv and input-3.csv: complete ledger flag and incoming quantities available
scope: CPU-only non-LLM forecasting; no policy optimization, neural models, reserved December outcomes or external research. October-November results are development evidence only.
measurement: Recorded-unit absolute error supports forecast selection, not savings or availability claims. Measure complete routine wall time and process peak RSS including preparation and retained model arrays. No paid model calls in routine. AI build cost requires unavailable usage/pricing.
